ops.title: Label path traversal: RecordPath bypasses validation, reachable from four exported deploy verbs
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.2a3 refuter, proved by measurement rather than argued.

A phase-4 pass introduced an `element` type so a path derivation cannot be written from a raw `Label`
without the launchd validation rule running. It landed at six sites. The seventh, `daemon.go:70`,
uses a raw conversion:

    func (d Daemon) RecordPath() string { return element(d.Label).record() }

`element(d.Label)` skips the rule. Measured:

    Label("../../evil").RecordPath() = "/var/folders/.../T/evil/daemon.records"  escapes-home = true
    Label(".hidden").RecordPath()    = ".../001/.hidden/daemon.records"
    Label("bin/daemon").RecordPath() = ".../001/bin/daemon/daemon.records"

And the path is READ: deploy/inventory.go:326-328 calls proc.ReadOwner on it, reachable from four
exported deploy verbs (deploy/inventory.go:298 requireEmpty ← deploy/deploy.go:267, :376, :457, and
deploy/quiesce.go:101). deploy.Open (deploy/deploy.go:120) validates only `Label != ""`.

NOT a regression — HEAD had zero validation at the same site. It is an incompleteness of the claimed
class fix, and the missed site is the only one an outside consumer can reach. The lane's own test
(`TestNoPathIsJoinedFromALabelLaunchdWouldRefuse`) enumerates seven doors and omits this one.

The exported godoc also claimed "it does no I/O and has no refusal to return: the file it names is
read past that rule or not at all" — the second clause is false.

DECISION (taken, not open): validate the Label at every boundary where a Daemon enters the library —
Serve via ValidateForServe, Open, and deploy.Open — so a Daemon that reached any code path is already
validated and RecordPath() on it is safe by construction. Rejected: panicking in RecordPath
(STYLEGUIDE reserves panic for the truly impossible, and consumer input reachable from four exported
verbs is not that), and keeping the exception silently.

ops.text: A hostile Label reaches no filesystem operation through any exported entry point that takes a Daemon
A table-driven test drives every hostile label through every such entry point and asserts nothing outside the state root is created, read, or stat'd
